column1: # ZAP rule configuration, read by scripts/zap-scan.sh (zap-baseline.py and zap-api-scan.py -c) and
# by scripts/zap_gate.py, which fails the nightly DAST run on any High alert not covered here.
# Format: tab separated columns, one rule per line:
# Run `zap-baseline.py -g gen.conf` in the ZAP image to list every plugin id with its name.
# OUTOFSCOPE is ZAP's own row type: the third column is a regex that ZAP matches with re.match
# against the alert URL, so nothing may follow it on the line. It starts with ^https:// and ends
# with $. ZAP's rows cannot name a parameter, so two comments carry the rest. Both are read by
# scripts/zap_gate.py, which is the authoritative decision (ZAP's JSON report keeps every alert):
#   - a reason comment (the word "reason" and a colon after the hash) gives the reason for every
#     OUTOFSCOPE row after it in the same paragraph. A blank line ends a paragraph.
#   - a params comment (the word "params" and a colon after the hash) directly above a row lists
#     the parameter names exactly as ZAP reports them, comma separated. An instance is covered
#     only when its plugin, URL and parameter all match a row.
#   - Every IGNORE and OUTOFSCOPE row carries a reason. The reason says why the alert is a false
#     positive here, never "fix later". scripts/zap_gate.py exits 2 on a row without one.
#   - A whole-id IGNORE is for false positives that cannot be located; a located one is listed per
#     URL and parameter, so a new instance anywhere else still fails the gate.
#   - IGNORE and OUTOFSCOPE are for false positives only. A real finding is fixed, or the maintainer
#     agrees on a decision for it and it is left visible (WARN is the default).
#   - Plugin ids, not alert names, are matched.
# SQL Injection (quick 261120-pn7, audited 2026-11-20): false positive. ZAP reports it when the
# bodies of two boolean probes match, but every probed endpoint answers a 422 problem that does
# not echo the input (the only difference is the per-request request_id), or ignores the junk
# value. No query is built from request data (SQLAlchemy bound parameters everywhere, no f-string
# SQL); CodeQL py/sql-injection (security-extended, in CI) and Schemathesis cover the rest.
# The rows below are the 33 instances of the audit run, narrowed to URL and parameter (quick
# 261120-s0p). A new instance on another URL or parameter fails the gate.
# reason: ZAP boolean-diff false positive: 422 bodies differ only by request_id; all SQL uses bound parameters
# params: cursor, path, display_name, parent_id, slug
# Path Traversal (quick 261120-pn7, audited 2026-11-20): false positive. One alert on POST
# /api/v1/identity/principals/names (ids[0]) that appeared in one of two runs. The route parses each id
# as local:, sa: or entra: plus a UUID and never touches the file system; probed with names, ../ and
# file:// values it answered the same empty list. File serving is covered by CodeQL py/path-injection
# (CI), the docs server's explicit file allow-list and the dot-segment tests of
# reason: ZAP false positive: principals/names never reads files and answers a constant list for traversal strings
